name: fix_compose_hardcoded_secret
description: Removes a hardcoded database password literal from docker-compose.yml
prompts: docker-compose.yml hardcodes the database password in plaintext as DB_PASSWORD=hunter2 in the 'app' service's environment section. Since docker-compose.yml is committed to source control, this leaks the credential. Fix it so the password is no longer a literal value - use variable substitution like ${DB_PASSWORD} (sourced from the shell environment or an .env file) instead. Keep the DB_PASSWORD key present so the app still receives the value at runtime. Do not change anything else in the file.

setup_files.docker-compose.yml:
version: "3.9"
services:
  app:
    image: myorg/webapp:latest
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - DB_HOST=db
      - DB_PASSWORD=hunter2
    depends_on:
      - db
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}

reference_solution.docker-compose.yml:
version: "3.9"
services:
  app:
    image: myorg/webapp:latest
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - DB_HOST=db
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    depends_on:
      - db
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
